high confidence. In Lemma 2.1 (Crop 7, [p3-7]), the RHS for the case $i 
eq j$ is given as $\prod_{k=0, k
eq j}^n (c_j - c_k)$. However, the LHS is $\psi'(c_j)$ where $\psi(x) = \prod_{k=0, k
eq i}^n (x - c_k)$. Evaluating $\psi'(c_j) = \sum_{m 
eq i} \prod_{k 
eq i, m} (c_j - c_k)$ at $x = c_j$ for $j 
eq i$ leaves only the term $m = j$, which equals $\prod_{k=0, k
eq i, j}^n (c_j - c_k)$ (as correctly written later in the proof in Eq. (2.7) / [p4-7]). Because the factor $(c_j - c_i)$ is included in $\prod_{k
eq j} (c_j - c_k)$, the stated expression in Lemma 2.1 differs from the LHS by an extra factor of $(c_j - c_i)$. Witness: \prod_{\substack{k=0 \ k
e i, j}}^{n} (c_j - c_k)
